skill.name: faceless
skill.description: Create, render, schedule, and publish AI faceless videos with Faceless.so. Manage scripts, captions, automated series, credits, connected accounts, calendars, and analytics.
skill.summary: Automate Faceless.so video creation, rendering, scheduling, publishing, and analytics.
skill.author: side-products

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives: API examples target Faceless.so, key references support authentication, and Markdown backticks are not Ruby execution. One unpinned npm execution risk is confirmed, and workflows lack explicit confirmation before credit charges or public posting.

remediation.issue: The setup runs the latest unpinned faceless-cli package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact trusted package version and integrity value. Require user confirmation before global installation or npx execution.

remediation.issue: Paid generation and public posting workflows lack a final confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Show cost, destination account, platform, schedule, and visibility. Require explicit approval before generation, publishing, or automatic series activation.

content.value_statement: Producing and distributing short videos across several platforms requires many coordinated steps. This skill guides Faceless.so creation, rendering, scheduling, publishing, and performance checks.
actual_capabilities: Create faceless videos from narration scripts with selected voices, models, styles, captions, and music.
Caption existing public video or audio files without generating new visuals.
Track asynchronous generation, render completed projects, and retrieve finished video links.
Publish immediately or schedule videos across connected social accounts.
Create, update, pause, generate, and monitor automated video series.
Check credits, accounts, posting calendars, available options, voices, and analytics.
limitations: Requires a Faceless.so account, API key, and sufficient credits for video generation.
The CLI requires Node.js 18 or later; the raw API is the fallback.
Captioning requires publicly reachable media URLs, and publishing requires connected social accounts.
Cloud generation and rendering are asynchronous and subject to service rate limits.

use_cases.title: Produce Short Videos
use_cases.description: Turn approved scripts into rendered faceless videos and prepare them for one social channel.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Social Publishing
use_cases.description: Schedule completed videos across connected platforms and review the posting calendar and performance.

use_cases.title: Automate Video Series
use_cases.description: Configure recurring topic-based episodes, monitor generation, and pause automation when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 60-second faceless video from this script. Use storyboard, show available voices first, and stop before spending credits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner video creation with a review point

prompt_templates.title: Render for YouTube
prompt_templates.prompt: Create and render this script, then prepare a YouTube Shorts post. Show the title, privacy, and credit cost before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Schedule Across Platforms
prompt_templates.prompt: Schedule video [ID] for YouTube and TikTok at [ISO time]. Verify accounts and metadata, then ask before scheduling.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Automated Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a weekday series about [topic] for [audience]. Compare model costs, propose settings, and require approval before creation or automatic posting.

output_examples.input: Create a storyboard video from my ocean facts script and stop before publishing.
output_examples.output: The storyboard video is complete and rendered. It used 20 credits. The draft YouTube title is ready for review; nothing was published.

output_examples.input: Schedule video 482 for YouTube and TikTok tomorrow at 18:00 UTC.
output_examples.output: Both accounts are connected and metadata is complete. The schedule is ready for approval for 18:00 UTC tomorrow.

output_examples.input: Summarize performance for the last 30 days.
output_examples.output: YouTube produced the most views, while TikTok had the strongest engagement rate. Two scheduled posts failed and need review.

best_practices: Confirm model cost, destination account, platform, schedule, and visibility before consequential actions.
Use structured command output and inspect the success field before continuing a workflow.
Verify scopes, connected accounts, and platform metadata before rendering, publishing, or scheduling.
anti_patterns: Do not install or execute an unpinned CLI package without user approval.
Do not publish, delete, or activate recurring posts from ambiguous instructions.
Do not continue polling after a completed or failed terminal status.

faq.question: What account access is required?
faq.answer: A Faceless.so API key is required. Publishing also requires connected social accounts and suitable key scopes.

faq.question: Does video generation consume credits?
faq.answer: Yes. Video creation and generated series episodes consume model-based credits. Rendering and publishing are described as free.

faq.question: Which platforms can receive posts?
faq.answer: The skill supports YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Threads when accounts are connected.

faq.question: Can it caption existing footage?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create captioned projects from publicly reachable video or audio URLs.

faq.question: Can it schedule several platforms together?
faq.answer: Yes. Each destination needs a connected account and complete platform metadata before scheduling.

faq.question: Does it upload local media files?
faq.answer: No direct local upload workflow is documented. Captioning and asset registration use publicly reachable media URLs.
